summary: Full e2e verification of the new Stripe subscription billing feature in Squawk King IA (backend + frontend). BACKEND (pytest, 10/10 pass): (1) GET /api/billing/plans public — 3 plans basic $19/5, pro $39/50, unlimited $79/null with trial_days=3; (2) admin (mechanic@squawkking.io) /billing/status = unlimited/allowed/active; (3) fresh registered user = plan trial, trial_active=true, trial_days_left=3, allowed=true, and CAN stream a chat message (no 402); (4) after backdating created_at 4 days, /billing/status flips to plan=none/allowed=false and POST /api/sessions/{id}/message returns HTTP 402 with detail 'Your free trial has ended. Choose a plan to continue troubleshooting.'; (5) Basic subscriber with tokens_used=5 returns 402 with 'token' in detail; (6) POST /api/payments/checkout for all 3 lookup keys returns a real https://checkout.stripe.com/... URL with cs_test_ session ID; GET /api/payments/status/{session_id} returns the pending shape; unknown lookup=400; unauth=401. FRONTEND (Playwright, 6 scenarios pass): (a) fresh register -> Workspace billing-badge shows 'Trial · 3d left'; clicking navigates to /pricing which renders plan-card-basic/pro/unlimited + subscribe-basic/pro/unlimited + 'Free trial · 3 days left' current-plan-line; (b) clicking subscribe-basic hits POST /api/payments/checkout and window.location redirects to https://checkout.stripe.com/... (Stripe hosted checkout page title 'Stripe Checkout' confirmed, sandbox banner visible, Card option renders 4242 4242 4242 4242 field, CVC 123, 12/34 accepted); (c) completing the hosted Stripe checkout end-to-end from the harness was not feasible in one shot (Stripe hosted flow requires Contact email + Billing address street/city + phone number for Link, which are stateful iframes) — per the review_request's explicit fallback, the paid path was exercised via a webhook-equivalent DB flip: /api/payments/status/{session_id} sync + apply_subscription set tier=basic/status=active; browser then visited /payment/success?session_id=<real cs_test_...> which polled and rendered data-testid=payment-confirmed 'You're on basic!', 'Enter the hangar' navigated to Workspace and the billing-badge updated to 'basic · 5 left'; (d) /payment/cancel renders payment-cancel-page 'Checkout canceled' with View plans / Back to app buttons; (e) expired-trial user (created_at -5d): billing-badge shows 'Trial ended', sending a chat message triggers 402 -> upgrade-modal opens with upgrade-reason 'Your free trial has ended. Choose a plan to continue troubleshooting.' and 3 plan cards + Choose buttons; (f) admin login shows billing-badge 'unlimited' (Plans on hover). AI features not in scope this iteration (billing/subscription only); regression: existing GPT-5.4 chat SSE still stream-works (used for trial-allowed test).
ai_feature_verdicts: not-in-scope-this-iteration - this iteration adds Stripe billing only; existing GPT-5.4 SSE chat was exercised as a sanity flow (trial user got a normal 200 stream).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py get_entitlement(): trial_days_left calculation uses `max(0, -(-int(secs) // 86400))` which is a ceiling, so a user 5 seconds into their trial still reads 3 days left. Cosmetic but harmless — considers changing to floor to be more accurate (a 71h-old trial should say '2d left' not '3d left').

server.py apply_subscription(): resets tokens_used=0 and period_start=now on every subscription apply. Fine on first purchase but if the same session is applied twice (webhook + inline poll race), the counter would reset. Idempotency guarded by payment_transactions.update_one({payment_status: {$ne: 'paid'}}) so the counter reset only runs once per session — good.

server.py /api/payments/checkout: `origin_url` is taken from client (window.location.origin) and interpolated into Stripe success_url/cancel_url. A malicious user could POST an arbitrary origin_url. Not a security break (Stripe just redirects to it on the client) but consider allow-listing to REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL / configured public URL server-side.

server.py /api/payments/status/{session_id} is unauthenticated and returns transaction status by session_id alone. Session IDs are unguessable so this is acceptable per typical Stripe integration patterns, but note that any actor with a session_id can trigger the apply_subscription side effect on first call — mitigation: current code only applies when Stripe.Session.retrieve says paid, so no risk of unauthorized tier grant. OK.

PricingPlans.jsx: subscribe() sets loadingKey only during checkout POST; on Stripe redirect it does window.location.href which unloads the page (fine). But on network failure, the toast is shown and loadingKey resets — good. Minor: no timeout on the checkout request; a slow Stripe call blocks the button silently.

Workspace.jsx billing-badge falls back to '…' while billing is loading. That is fine, but consider a skeleton or `Loading` label — the ellipsis reads oddly to a user seeing it for the ~200ms load. (Automated tests must poll — added `wait for not '…'` in scripts.)
PaymentSuccess.jsx polls /payments/status every 2s up to 12 polls (~24s). If the webhook is delayed >24s, user sees 'Still processing' which is graceful. Good UX.

server.py: stripe SDK's `managed_payments={enabled: True}` is used first, then fallback to `automatic_tax + billing_address_collection='required'`. Both paths verified to produce a real cs_test_ session. The tax fallback path forces address collection which makes the hosted checkout slightly heavier — acceptable for a compliance MVP.
server.py CheckoutRequest: no length/URL validation on origin_url. If a client passes a very long or malformed URL it will 500 on Stripe. Consider Pydantic HttpUrl.

Frontend: chat 402 handling in ChatPanel.jsx lines 111–121 removes the tmp user message using `tmp-${Date.now()}` — Date.now() ran on the setMessages create AND on the filter, so the timestamps differ by a few ms and the filter never matches. The optimistic user bubble stays in the transcript when the paywall opens (visible in the upgrade-modal screenshot). Not blocking, but the pattern is buggy: capture the tmp id once (const tmpId = `tmp-${Date.now()}`) and reuse.

success_rate.backend: 100% (10/10 pytest test_billing.py + earlier backend_test.py suite still passing per iteration_3 note)

test_credentials: mechanic@squawkking.io / squawk123 (admin, treated as unlimited). Throwaway registered users used per scenario; all cleaned up post-run.
seed_data_creation: Created and cleaned up: trialui2_*, paid2_*, paidsim_*, expired_* throwaway users. Deleted all payment_transactions rows created during the run.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Billing selectors verified: billing-badge (sidebar, opens /pricing), plan-card-{basic|pro|unlimited}, subscribe-{basic|pro|unlimited}, current-plan-line, upgrade-modal, upgrade-modal-close, upgrade-reason, payment-success-page, payment-confirmed, go-to-app, payment-cancel-page, back-to-app. To simulate expired trial: db.users.update_one({email},{'$set':{'created_at': (now-5d).isoformat()}}). To simulate paid tier without driving Stripe UI: db.payment_transactions.update_one({session_id},{'$set':{'payment_status':'paid'}}) + apply_subscription equivalent (tier/subscription_status='active'/tokens_used=0/period_start=now on users). Backdate + relogin (or wait for /billing/status refresh) to see badge changes. To test the token-limit paywall via UI, set tokens_used>=5 with tier=basic and subscription_status=active. NOTE (bug found): ChatPanel.jsx 402 handling does not remove the optimistic user bubble because the tmp id is re-computed with Date.now() — user bubble lingers in the transcript when the upgrade modal opens. Reported under critical_code_review_comments; non-blocking. Full end-to-end Stripe hosted checkout with test card 4242 was NOT completable in one Playwright run due to required Contact email + Billing address + phone iframes — do NOT count that as a bug; use the DB-flip fallback the review request calls out.
rca of the issue: N/A — billing feature verified working end-to-end; only minor code-quality observations flagged.
